owner: CC (code + proofs); Akien (the intention, and the scope ruling of 2026-07-30: 'import root + the verb', build-minimal, deferring host-seam verification and repair to a later rung)
intention: THE LAUNCHER BRINGS UP THE FLOOR IT NEEDS, THEN TELLS CLAUDE WHAT IT COULD NOT FIX. superclaude stops being a thing that only starts Claude Code and becomes the thing that starts Claude Code WITH AS MANY OF THE PARTS ALREADY WORKING AS IT CAN MANAGE: a venv in instance-space, an editable install so `cairn` imports from any directory, and every declared dependency actually present. Whatever it cannot repair rides into the session on --append-system-prompt, complete enough to act on, so the session opens already knowing rather than discovering. And the question that started it — 'how do I run a proof here?' — gets an ADDRESS: `cairn test`, registered with the dispatcher that already lists its own verbs.
why: Akien, 2026-07-30, watching a session burn four tool calls finding out how to run one proof: 'we're not selecting a pre-built venv before getting started... so if a venv is not built, you spend tokens sorting that over and over. Tokens spent and not compiled.' And on the report half: 'it does what it can, then reports to claude if there are problems so Claude can get them fixed. it's part of the tool becomes invisible when you use it.' Both halves are Law 1: an answered question that did not become structure gets re-derived, and re-derivation is the defect — whether the re-deriver is a human or the next session.
traces_to: Law 1 (the resolver is spent on the novel, not on re-deriving the settled) — the whole ticket
Law 3 (nothing is known until measured) — the floor is verified by importing, never assumed from a stamp
Law 4 (a rule that matters is enforced by physics) — the undeclared-import rule became a proof, not prose
Law 7 (loud at diagnostic surfaces, permanent in records of truth) — the verb reports and seals nothing
the rescue ethos (launchers/intention+why.json) — the tier below the machinery, which must work when the machinery does not

gates.BUILDME: the seam exists, is sourced by superclaude, and cannot abort a launch
gates.PROVEME: launchers/proofs/test_bootstrap.py (14 cases) and cairn/tester/proofs/test_cli.py (8 cases) both green, and the whole suite no worse than before

falsifier: The floor can be reported UP while `import cairn` from outside the repo actually fails; OR the preflight can prevent Claude Code from starting; OR `cairn test` can report green without a proof having actually passed (including green over ZERO proofs).
horizon: A host-seam's seal EXPIRES by construction — the venv lives where git cannot see it, so the host drifts with nothing in this repo changing. launchers/proofs/test_bootstrap.py IS the re-runnable verify; a green means the floor was up when it last ran, not that it is up now.
dependencies: cairn/tester/device.py — run_proof is the real door the verb routes through, so green here means green there
bin/cairn — the dispatcher that makes `test` an address rather than a docstring
provenance: Born 2026-07-30 from a measurement taken on the session that opened that morning: four tool calls (`cairn test` — the right address, empty; pytest — nothing in this repo uses it; a module path — absent; then reading the proof's docstring) to answer a settled question. Underneath it sat a defect nobody had caught since 2026-07-15: pyproject asserted '`pip install -e .` stays green at all times' while the install had never been performed, `cairn` imported only because cwd happened to be the repo root, and PEP 668 refuses that install into system python outright — so the promise could not have been kept where it was being made.

PROVEME.need: the live floor is measured by importing from a cwd that is NOT the repo root
a broken preflight still reaches Claude Code, carrying its report
the proof is non-vacuous — the in-situ half genuinely reds on a down floor
PROVEME.how_measured: CAIRN_VENV=/proc/cairn-no-such-dir/venv python3 launchers/proofs/test_bootstrap.py -> exit 1, exactly the 4 in-situ cases fail, the 10 mechanism cases correctly still pass

watchme: NONE, BECAUSE the residual question is not measurable from class-space, and the honest answer is to say so rather than to spec a watch that cannot be emitted. What this seam raises over time is: does a floor that was REPORTED broken actually get FIXED — i.e. does the report reaching Claude close the loop Akien named? That question is answered only by launch records in instance-space (~/.cairn/logs/preflight.json), and the probe berthing doctrine's destination (ii) — an instance-space probe — remains authored doctrine with NO WORKED EXAMPLE (filed by watchme-emits-a-probe, 2026-07-30). Carrying a watch I cannot emit would be exactly the silence the emission gate exists to refuse, wearing a spec's clothes. Two things kept this from becoming an excuse: the ONE residual question that WAS answerable from class-space — 'does the declared dependency set stay true as imports are added?' — was made PHYSICS instead of a watch (test_every_third_party_import_is_declared), because a watch on a question you can already answer is waiting to learn what you could measure; and the instance-space edge is filed below rather than dropped.

forwarding.pyproject.toml::dependencies: was `[]` while cairn/db_domain/ imported psycopg2 — now declares psycopg2-binary>=2.9, with the why in-file
forwarding.pyproject.toml::'pip install -e . stays: the claim is unchanged in wording and TRUE for the first time; the comment beneath it now records that it was false from 2026-07-15 to 2026-07-30 and why it could not have been true

distinctions_recorded: A DOCSTRING IS NOT AN ADDRESS. The answer to 'how do I run a proof' was correctly written down — inside the proof file, which you can only read once you have already found it, which is the thing you were trying to do. Compiling an answer means putting it where the question is ASKED (the dispatcher), not where the answer is true.

A PROBE IS FOR A QUESTION THAT NEEDS TIME; A PROOF IS FOR ONE THAT DOES NOT. The undeclared-import rule was a candidate watch and became a proof instead — it is deterministically answerable from files in git, so watching for it would be waiting to discover something already knowable.
A VENV IS RUNTIME STATE. It went to ~/.cairn, never the repo. The tell is decisive and general: a thing that would need gitignoring is a thing in the wrong root.

A HINT THAT NAMES A CAUSE IT DID NOT MEASURE IS WORSE THAN SILENCE. Measured 2026-07-30: the venv-create finding read 'usually the missing ensurepip package' while the actual error was ENOENT on the parent directory. Now the measured output leads and everything after it is labelled a candidate — and there is a regression case pinning that.

REPRODUCIBILITY OVER OFFLINE CLEVERNESS. --system-site-packages was considered and refused: it would have satisfied psycopg2 from the host with no download, but it makes the floor's contents a function of what the box happens to have — the exact hypothesis that caused the defect.
filed_edges: INSTANCE-SPACE PROBE, UNBUILT: the preflight writes ~/.cairn/logs/preflight.json on every launch and nothing reads it. Whether reported-but-unfixed floors actually get fixed is unmeasured, and measuring it needs probe destination (ii), which has no worked example. This is the honest content of the watchme 'none, because X' above.

THE REPORT IS A LAUNCH-TIME SNAPSHOT. It rides --append-system-prompt, so it persists for the whole session even after the floor is repaired mid-session. Acceptable today because it says it was measured at launch; a stale claim in a long session is the failure mode to watch.

SCOPE RULED OUT BY AKIEN, NOT FORGOTTEN: verifying and repairing the OTHER host-seams at launch (postgres reachable, sudo_relay up, bwrap present for the tester's isolation). The preflight's shape takes them without redesign — each is another finding appended by verify.
